slides.title: Most day-to-day fiber work happens above ground.
slides.body: Where you place the enclosure affects every service call for twenty years.

slides.title: Pedestals: small and cheap
slides.body: Knee-high enclosures holding a splice closure, a multiport terminal or drop slack. The workhorse of residential builds.

slides.title: Their enemy: mowers
slides.body: Trimmers, snow ploughs and reversing cars find pedestals. Place them at property lines, clear of driveways and car doors.

slides.title: Cabinets hold the hub
slides.body: In a PON, the cabinet houses the fiber distribution hub: feeder fibers, 1:32 splitters and patch panels.

slides.title: Every cabinet needs
slides.body: A ground rod, a lock, ventilation that keeps water out, and a plinth above flood and snow levels.

slides.title: Other countries, other boxes
slides.body: India uses pole or wall-mounted FAT boxes. Australia puts hubs in footpath cabinets and terminals in pits.

items: The door opens away from traffic
